desc:
The valley bottom is covered in rocks and debris which have broken from the
mountain and come tumbling down to end up here. The valley bends here to the
north and east, or you can climb the mountain to the west.
name: In a Valley

desc:
Rocks from above lie strewn all over the floor, some large rocks, some small.
Most look like they have been lying here for many years, ravaged by wind and
rain. The valley bends west and south; to the east a smaller valley climbs up
towards a narrow gap in the Hithaeglir.
name: In a Valley

desc:
The trail you are following leads east and west here. Westwards you can see
mountains rising to high peaks, while to the east you can see the wide valley of
the Anduin. In the far north you spot an area of darkness which may herald a
forest of some sort, but you can't be sure from this distance. Still in the
north but rather closer you see a path winding its way east to west.
name: Narrow Gap

desc:
Here is the lowest part of a slippery and steep path through the mountain. It is
only possible to travel north. Some lichens grows here but else this place is
deserted of any form of permanent life.
name: Steep Path

desc:
The valley continues north and south here. Picking your way carefully through
shattered rocks, you wonder if you will ever find a way out of here.. when
suddenly you spot a trail leading up the side of the mountain to the west. All
around you can look up and see the magnificent snow-capped peaks towering high
above you.
name: In a Valley

desc:
A rock wall towers up on the east, casting its long shadow over the valley
floor. In the west you can start to climb up the side of one of the tallest
peaks in this range, or you can follow this barren valley either north or south.
name: In a Valley

desc:
The valley ends here, dropping so sharply to the south that it would be folly to
even try going down it. You can climb the mountains to the west, where you see
the highest peak you have ever beheld rising far above your head, or you can
follow the valley northwards. To the east a tall cliff blocks your way.
name: In a Valley

desc:
Travel further south is curtailed by a large outcrop of rocks, which is almost
impossible to pass. You can however descend into a valley to the east, or climb
back up the mountain in the west.
name: On a Mountainside

desc:
Standing on the loose rocks you wonder if this was a wise move, but the ground
underfoot seems to be solid enough for the moment. You can traverse the side of
the mountain to the north or south, descend to a valley in the east, or climb up
to a ridge on the top of the mountain in the west.
name: On a Mountainside

desc:
The rocks on this side of the mountain are loose, but not loose enough to make
you lose your balance and fall. You can descend further into the valley bottom,
traverse the mountainside to the south, or climb back up to the ridge in the
north or west.
name: On a Mountainside

desc:
This small enclosed yard lies adjacent to a crude homestead, and obviously
provides shelter to a few of the animals kept by whomever dwells in the cabin.
The only fencing is along the northern edge of the pen - in every other
direction natural granite forms the sides.
name: Animal Pen

desc:
This very old road was once built by dwarves to support trade between Arnor and
the Lonely Mountain. Now it is mainly used by foul creatures of the night. The
road leads north and south passing a slope you can see if you look west. On the
east side is a green but very dark forest.
name: Old Dwarven Road

desc:
The old road turns north and east here. To the east of the road the forest is so
thick that you can barely see two steps ahead. To the west the pine-forest rises
almost to the top of the mountain slope.
name: Bend in the Old Dwarven Road

desc:
This is yet another turn in the twisting road, which is getting more and more
overgrown. Obviously, travellers are not common guests here. Maybe the
inhabitants of the surrounding forests do not need tracks or roads?
name: Old Dwarven Road

desc:
The road bends north and east here. Green hills rise to the west of the road,
their slopes covered by various trees and bushes. Some tall birches grow just to
the south of the road. To the northeast you can see a dark forest.
name: Old Dwarven Road

desc:
Zigzagging its way through a dark forest, this overgrown road can take you into
the Misty Mountains, or south towards the Anduin. On all sides, high trees
surrounds you.
name: Old Dwarven Road

desc:
The road makes its way through a very dark forest. It is possible to continue on
the road north and east. A thick forest to the south does not let anyone pass.
The trees to the west are less dense.
name: Old Dwarven Road

desc:
The road makes its way through a dark forest towards an unknown destiny in the
east. Looking along the road, you can see that it leads down to the river
Anduin, which it crosses by a ford, known to be rather dangerous. Beyond the
river the road leads into Mirkwood and to the lands beyond.
name: Road to the Old Ford

desc:
The trees that stand here are worn and scarred, like weary soldiers after a
bloody battle. Many other trees lie on the ground; some have been cut, some
broken, and some uprooted altogether. Smaller branches and twigs litter the
area, with dead leaves and wood splinters covering the earth. As the wind blows
by, it creates a low, resonating sound, with the pitch shifting up as the wind
dies down. This place looks like a battlefield, as if the forces of nature had
met in some sort of violent clash, only to have a tragic finale ending in sorrow
and despair.
name: Bleeding Forest

desc:
The forest here thins, allowing much more light to enter compared to the darker
surrounding forest. Most of the trees seem to have been growing here a long
while, although some are younger, about twice as tall as an adult human. The
lower density of the forest gives room for some shrubs to grow. Some of the
bushes have little round berries, although they do not look like they would be
very tasty. The foliage all around has a medium green hue, but there is a great
variety in the shapes of the leaves.
name: Light Forest

desc:
The river makes a bend here, turning east. Upstream to the north the river is
cloaked in the darkness of the forest. On this new eastward course light can be
seen; a refreshing change from the dreary forest. As the river turns against the
bank it quickly picks up speed, the sound of the churning water drowns out any
noise of wildlife; thunder is perhaps the only thing that might be heard over
the water.
name: Swift Forest River

desc:
Free of the dark forest, the river is wider and more approachable. From the
grassy banks the slow trickle of water can be heard. At this point, the river
turns southward. The rocks in the riverbed are worn smooth and round from
decades of the water running slowly over them. The surrounding plains have been
soaked by the rivers' runoff.
name: Emerging River

desc:
As the river bends towards the south it widens slightly. Although slow flowing
up until this point the slope of the ground to the south-east pulls the water
downstream more forcefully. The current is increasingly stronger as it rushes to
meet the much larger Anduin River in the distance. The shadow of the forest to
the west is now just a memory, as this river heads toward brighter plains and
pastures.
name: Small River

desc:
As the river bends eastward the current begins to pick up speed. While the
northern portion of this segment of river is relatively calm, the eastern
section rushes at quite a quick pace. The fervent sounds of rushing water can be
heard coming from that direction. Westward a dark forest looms, casting an
ominous shadow upon the land.
name: Turn in the River

desc:
The river slows a bit here as it turns to the south, but it is not by any means
tranquil. Looking upstream to the west there is a dark forest in the distance.
Toward the east there are some ruins of what could have been a house, now
reduced to rubble. Whatever destroyed that place is unknown. However, it was
certainly not natural erosion.
name: Fast Flowing River

desc:
At this bend the river makes a quick turn backward to the east, part of a series
of turns that serve to speed up the current even more. The loud roar of the
rushing water is overwhelming and the banks of the river are under tremendous
pressure as they force the strong river to turn at a sharp angle. Anyone
travelling by boat here would have to keep their focus as they navigate these
waters, lest they be dashed against the banks or capsized by the force of the
water. A swimmer could do nothing but let the strongest current carry him where
it may.
name: Bend in the River

desc:
As the river travels eastwards it roughly brushes against the riverbank, which
serves to turn its course to the south. As it rubs against the bank the flow of
the water begins to slow. Ahead in the distance the river is just a calm, smooth
trickle.
name: A Turn in the River

desc:
The river is calm as it moves slowly eastwards away from the shadow of the
mountains in the west. Small water insects can be seen skimming the surface of
the water along with broken bits of reeds that float gently past. A sense of
peacefulness exudes from the small eddy pools formed by rocks in the current,
and the soothing sound of the waters gentle flow.
name: Tributary of the River

desc:
The forest surrounding you is very old. Ancient trees loom above you, forming an
impenetrable ceiling between you and the sky. Moss-covered stones and the
remnants of long dead trees make it very hard to move.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
The trees in this area of the forest seem younger than in other parts of it, but
still have weathered many seasons. Their lush foliage blocks out any natural
sunlight. The floor of the forest consists mostly of fallen leaves and twigs.
Smaller plants and shrubs would be choked out by the massive roots of the
towering trees, and would not receive the light they need to survive. The same
might be true for other things that enter here.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
The forest is thick as the trees crowd each other. The trees are an even mixture
of old, wizened ones and younger, less hardened ones. With the passing wind the
tree branches sway, looking as if they are talking to each other; it is almost
possible to hear them whispering.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
Despite the great darkness covering much of this entire area, here some light
from the sky manages to break through. The illumination is enough to see clearly
during the day, or with a full moon at night. The stands of trees, while
predominantly young, include some larger, older trees as well. The unusual quiet
of this place, coupled with the uneven shafts of light entering from above,
combine to create a very eerie feeling suggesting this would not make a good
resting place.
name: Mixed Forest

desc:
In this part of the forest there is a great variety among the trees. Some seem
to be quite old, having weathered many winters, and grown tall with the light of
the spring. Others are shorter, but still seem as if they have been here for
ages. If only one could know what these trees have seen, for surely they must
have been growing here since the beginning of time.
name: Mixed Forest

desc:
Several large trees stand around this glade, providing a natural cloak. The
ground is worn and packed, as if many large and heavy creatures had travelled
through here. Some trees bear large scratches like scars, evidence that some of
the visitors were quite fierce creatures with large, sharp claws. If those
creatures were marking their territory it might be unwise to stay here for long
lest they return.
name: Wolf Glade

desc:
The forest is more dense. High trees mixed with lower brush form a very hard
terrain to move in. Looking around you, you see the tracks of wild animals such
boars and deers. You also see tracks of something bigger - man or beast...
Looking back, you get the comforting view of the road to the south and the west
and realise that at least you are not hopelessly lost yet.
name: Thick Forest

desc:
This dark and gloomy forest covers some of the foothills of the Misty mountains.
Somewhere to the east, the land gradually flattens into the Vale of Anduin, but
here it is still quite rugged.
name: Thick Forest

desc:
The thick undergrowth is making it hard to walk. To the north the forest is so
dense that you can barely see two steps ahead. The trees grow less dense south
and west.
name: Thick Forest

desc:
Trees surround you on all the sides, hiding the sky above. The forest is dark
and gloomy with thick undergrowth, making it very hard to move around. All
around you, you hear the sounds of the forest, birds singing and boars grunting.
name: Deep inside the Forest

desc:
To the north and to the east you can see nothing but tall green trees. West and
south you can catch a glimpse of an overgrown road making its way through the
forest.
name: Dark Green Forest

desc:
Under an overhanging cliff, there is a dirty, smelly, stinking orc camp among
sharp rocks. Filthy piles of debris lies around it, and some unsanitary pots
with black, oily stews can be seen hanging over fires.
name: Orc Camp

desc:
You have now reached the bottom of the valley. A few bushes and some grass cover
the slopes, feeding the few animals that dwell here. The mountain slopes bear
footmarks of humanoid beings.
name: Vale in the Hithaeglir

desc:
Rocks again... what a surprise. The rough path you are following along the side
of this mountain makes a bend to the east and south here: to the east the path
descends to the bottom of a valley, while to the south it enters a narrow
canyon. Mountains rise up majestically in the north and west, but you can spot
no way of climbing them from here.
name: The Mountainside

desc:
You are on the bottom of a rocky canyon, about two meters wide. High, smooth
cliffs, with no handholds in sight, flank you on both sides, leaving almost no
choice on where to proceed: you can either follow the canyon to the north, or
squeeze through a crevice westwards.
name: Narrow Canyon

desc:
Wow! The view from here is breathtaking. You have reached one of the lower
eastern ridges of the Misty Mountains. Looking east, you see a green forest and
beyond it the mighty Anduin with its surrounding lowlands. Even further away
lies a dark-green sea, the Mirkwood. To the west you see a deep valley far
below.
name: Mountain Ridge

desc:
The ridge turns west-south here. To the west you can see its crest and the
snow-capped peaks of the mountains beyond. To the east and the north you can try
to make your way down the rocky slopes to the green valleys below.
name: Mountain Ridge

desc:
You are climbing up the steep rocky slope to the top of the mountain ridge. The
rough path, which has been leading up the slope, has disappeared. The bushes and
the long grasses between the boulders, the patches of rabbit-cropped turf and
the bright flowers have all vanished. Pebbles, rubbish, rocks and boulders cover
the slope in uneven piles, as if waiting for something or someone to start an
avalanche.
name: Mountain Slope

desc:
You are on the slope which leads to the top of a mountain ridge. A few bushes
are the only larger growing things here. A small forest can be seen below the
ridge to the east.
name: Mountain Slope

desc:
You are on the top of a wide steep slope of fallen stones, the remains of a
landslide. When you try to move down it, rubbish and small pebbles roll away
from your feet. Soon larger bits of split stone go clattering down and start
other pieces below them slithering and rolling, and you are forced to walk very
carefully to avoid setting the whole slope above and below you on the move.
name: Top of the Mountain Slope

desc:
You have finally reached the eastern and lower side of the ridge. Looking around
you, you see the Misty Mountains to the west, and a small forest below you to
the northeast. A few dwarf birches are the only growing things up here except
for the low grass that covers the ridge.
name: Mountain Ridge

desc:
You have stumbled across a small path among the rocks. It leads east, from where
you can hear thick voices speaking a foul orkish dialect.
name: Rocky Path

desc:
Slender white birches rise all around you, a marvel in this dully coloured
landscape. To the north and east you can see the old dwarven road running along
the border of a dense forest. The ground is very wet. To the west there is an
opening between the trees that does not look natural.
name: Birches

desc:
You have reached the crest of the ridge. The steep mountain slopes facing west,
south and north make this place look like a fortress. The air is thin and clear,
and even the smell of the pine trees does not reach so far up in the mountains.
During the short and intense spring, the mountain flowers celebrate it with
colours and smells.
name: Crest of the Ridge

desc:
This forest, on the eastern foothills of the Misty Mountains consists mainly of
high, strong pines, mixed with an occasional birch and some oaks. Every step you
take brings you further up on the mountains, that rise to heights of over
eighteen thousand feet above you.
name: Small Forest

desc:
You are on the edge of a climbing wood of pines that stand here right up the
mountain slope from the deeper darker forests of the valleys below. Looking
west, you can see the rocky slope continue till it reaches the top of the
mountain ridge. A path goes down the slope to the south.
name: Edge of a Small Forest

desc:
You are on the edge of a green pine forest at the eastern foothills of the
largest mountain-range in all Arda - the Misty Mountains. Just east of here you
can barely make out a small road. To the west the terrain starts to slope up.
Some tracks lead south.
name: Pine Forest

desc:
The slope is covered with fir trees that provide some shelter from the wind. To
the north you can see the top of a cliff and a series of waterfalls below. To
the east, the trees give way to a road, and beyond the road there is a dense
forest. To the west the ground becomes more rocky.
name: Slope above a Stream

desc:
Rocks of all possible shapes and sizes are strewn around you. A couple of fir
trees decorate the monotonous landscape. To the east, the ground slopes up a
little. To the north there is a steep drop to a small stream. To the south the
slope rises all the way to the crest of the mountain ridge.
name: Rocky Plains

desc:
The path turns west-south here, rising up the rocky slope to the south. Pebbles
and lumps of rock litter the path, making it hard to move. Some boulders rise on
the sides of the path, giving a shelter from the wind and falling rocks to a few
patches of grass and an occasional bright flower. To the north you can see a
small stream.
name: Rough Path

desc:
The path leaves the small dell to the north and winds its way up the green
slope. Bushes and boulders seem to be all around you, both beside the path and
almost directly under your feet, as if trying to make you stumble. You notice
some plants and berries which look as if they might be edible.
name: Rough Path

desc:
At the centre of a large circle, formed by some old firs, stands an ancient oak
tree. The knots on its trunk seem to form a face, as if it were grimly looking
out at the world. Its boughs rise towards the sky, like an evil priest might
raise his arms in chanting words of doom. Every now and then, as the wind blows,
the other trees sway, like a great crowd in an uproar.
name: Gathering of the Trees

desc:
The surface of the road is somewhat bumpy with small patches of grass growing
among the rough stones. If one looks carefully, traces of aged wagon tracks can
still be seen in the hard clay. The road runs from the west, where a dark forest
looms, southward to the dim outline of a mountain range on the horizon.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
The surface of the road is somewhat bumpy with small patches of grass growing
among the rough stones. If one looks carefully aged wagon tracks can be seen in
the sections covered by hard clay. The road runs from the north, where a small
river is still visible, to the south, where a mountain stands.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The craggy ground has a rugged surface littered with numerous small rocks. A few
remaining bulky stumps are scattered across the ground giving the impression
that a forest existed here a long time ago. The ground slopes gently to the east
where the soil has fewer rocks. Bypassing this area to the south and west is an
unused-looking road.
name: Rough Plains

desc:
The road turns sharply here, skirting a gently rising slope to the south-west.
The terrain towards the east and north, which holds numerous young saplings,
contains the remains of an old forest. Further south-west a tremendous mountain
overshadows the surrounding lands.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
West of the road the ground rises sharply towards a tall mountain while the
ground slowly ascends to the south. East of the road there is a grove of young
saplings growing among the rotten tree stumps of a former forest. The road
continues both south and north.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
This area was once a vast forest but was cut down long ago. A large number of
rotten tree stumps are visible, many of them now serving as homes for termites
and grubs. Among the stumps a new forest of young saplings grows.
name: Tangled Cutting Grounds

desc:
Various kinds of slender young trees form a thick and exuberant grove here. The
soil is dank and fertile with a lot of small undergrowth struggling beneath the
trees. A few hoary stubs of large trees are scattered in sections, cut down by
woodsmen long ago. An old forest road is visible southward, being rarely used
now that the major woods have diminished.
name: Cramped Grove

desc:
The road makes a gentle turn here, continuing to the west and south. A grove
with lush vegetation is located to the north. To the east there is a large
strange-looking hollow, filled with bushes and covered by a soft mist. It
appears that this road is infrequently travelled upon from the state of the
roadbed.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
Thick bushes fill this large hollow which was formed long ago by some mystical
event of the sky. The soil here is obviously saturated because groundwater
easily rises when even the smallest of creatures walks upon it. The air is very
humid and a deep mist forms from the ground. A clearing, cloaked in haze, opens
to the north.
name: Misty Hollow

desc:
A strange-looking hollow covered with haze and thick bushes lies on the north
side of the road and is the source of the mist that covers this region. East of
here the ground descends to a large plain of rich soil. The road continues to
the south and west.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
This vast plain has low vegetation that spreads out to the north. An extensive
vale with the Anduin river at its centre can be seen from here when the light is
right. The region to the north-west appears bushier than the valley while a
road, probably used by the Woodmen of long ago, lies to the south and west.
name: Vast Plain

desc:
The old forest road runs to the east and north while a muddy trail joins it from
the south. The trail has a rough surface and appears to be rarely used. To the
east the road continues until it is out of sight. A tall grass covers the ground
on the west side of the road.
name: Fork in the Road

desc:
The surface of this trail has been formed by layers of mud that have hardened
during the dry spells between rains. Depressions from wagons are barely
detectable in the battered ground. The eastern edge of the trail is overlaid
with large bushes, while the area to the west looks grassy. The trail continues
both to the north and the south.
name: Muddy Trail

desc:
Grass covers the land that borders this loam trail. Its infrequent usage seems
to be only by wandering animals. The trail declines slightly to the south where
it later turns westward. Far in the north the trail connects to a wider road
that is in better condition.
name: Muddy Trail

desc:
This plain seems very lively having an abundance of vegetation consisting of
grass several feet high and various kinds of flowers. Several small bushes with
small, green leaves have also managed to take root in the excellent soil. A
mud-covered trail to the east and south bypasses this plain.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
A few burdock bushes are scattered among the clovers that cover this placid
plain. A trail of matted grass and lumps of excrement marks the frequent passage
of large animals across these plains. An entrance to a burned village is located
southward.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
Grass, about a foot tall, covers this land which is next to an old road running
along the south side of here. The land is low and continues a smooth descent
eastwards where the fertile ground is filled with many different types of
flowering plants. A wide valley, filled with various vegetation, opens to the
north where the plant life seems to flourish.
name: Grass beside the Road

desc:
This grassy land contains an even mix of hay and bushes with a few molehills
scattered about. The surrounding lands look the same except to the east where
the bushes grow more densely.
name: Grassland

desc:
The grassy land gently slopes down towards the west where a muddy-looking trail
leads towards a village in the distant west. Hummocks of trefoil can be seen
growing in several places forming a quilt-like pattern before you. The grassy
land continues in all directions but the west.
name: Grassland

desc:
The rough trail bends here continuing to the north and the west where the
remains of a burned village stand. It appears that the trail has not been used
in a long time because of the rampant growth of hay which now covers it. The
ground ascends slightly towards the east where a wide spread of grassland lies.
name: Bend in Muddy Trail

desc:
Plains covered with grass and a few bushes surround this muddy trail which rises
gently towards a burned village standing in the west. The mud on this trail
could show the tracks of animals but the settling and flowing of the mud on this
slope eventually removes them.
name: Muddy Trail

desc:
This spot, where the land rises towards the ruined yard of a burned down
village, marks the head of a muddy trail. The walls which once protected this
village from its enemies are now crumbling and the wooden gateway which stood
between the walls has been smashed. The remains of a burned out guard tower can
be found southwards.
name: Entrance to the Burned Down Village

desc:
A burned down village stands east of these dry plains. The plain appears very
barren with only a small amount of vegetation, consisting mainly of a few small
stunted bushes and some short grass. Traces of some animals can be seen on the
softer spots of the ground when they pass through.
name: Drought Stricken Land

desc:
Although the soil here is withered, small patches of grass and a few short
bushes still manage to grow. It seems that the vegetation becomes more lush to
the east, while the land to the north looks rocky and barren. Towards the south
stands what was once a sturdy stone wall, but it is now falling apart.
name: Scrubby Plains

desc:
Numerous rocks of various sizes litter the ground, forming a patchy carpet of
stone. A few parched branches squeeze their way through the rocks, reaching for
light. To the north a mountain trail declines to here. The soil softens towards
the east and south while the rocky land continues to the west.
name: Rocky Land

desc:
The terrain slopes gently down towards a pond some twenty feet wide and filled
with squalid-looking water. A few lily pads lie on the surface of the water, and
various stones, covered with caustic phlegm, form a border around the pond.
Tracks of various animals are embedded upon the muddy ground.
name: Slimy Pond

desc:
The rich soil of this land is bountiful with dense hay. During the warm summer
months various kinds of flowers burst with health, creating a richly-coloured
environment. There are some smooth little stones scattered about and several
small holes in the ground, most likely dug by moles.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
Large bushes, with thick leaves, grow on this sharp bank which borders a road to
the north. Some of the bushes are missing leaves, having been consumed by
insects and herbivores which occupy the luxuriant terrain. The ground descends
gently southward where it is covered by grass and a few bushes. To the west
there is a muddy trail which joins the road in the north-west.
name: Bushy Bank

desc:
The ground here is covered with numerous bushes of various sizes and types. All
of the bushes look healthy though some of the branches have been gnawed by
animals feeding in this area. The bushy embankment continues westward and runs
parallel to the road just north of here while the lands to the east and south
are covered with grass.
name: Bushy Bank

desc:
Short parched grass grows on this otherwise uninhabited plain. The once soft
ground has become rather dried and broken due to long periods of sunshine and
infrequent rain. The land rises gently northward where a bushy embankment
stands. Grasslands continue to the south and west while a small clearing among
the bushes is visible to the east.
name: Loamy Grassland

desc:
A muddy trail bypasses this grassy field to the west. Here, the ground is very
rough and supports some divergent flowers and a few insignificant bushes. The
ground gently rises northward where it forms an embankment covered with bushes.
The grass continues to the east and south.
name: Grassland

desc:
Towards the east the road descends until it joins the mouth of a very large
valley, while to the west the road continues until it branches north and south.
On the south side of the road there is an embankment that is covered by large
bushes. On the north side of the road lies a vast plain with short grass growing
on it.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
An embankment, containing various types of bushes, lies to the south side of
this infrequently used road. The road descends towards the east. North of the
road is a grassy area. The road itself looks to be very old and in poor shape
after having been deeply rutted by the passage of wagons many years ago.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Short and dry grass covers this barren plain which contains only a few small
bushes and some large rocks. Bones of some small animals are scattered around
and other traces of different kinds of animals are imprinted on the surface.
name: Drought Stricken Land

desc:
This barren land supports only a few stunted bushes and a couple of feeble
pines. Very little grass has managed to take root in this poor soil. Towards the
east the land becomes more hospitable to vegetation and more grass can be seen.
A battered stonewall stands to the south-east, separating a burned down village
from these barren lands. The region to the north appears very rugged.
name: Scrubby Lowland

desc:
The ground here is rugged and lifeless, with a few broken stones littered across
the top and an occasional dead root embedded in the surface. The bones of
several small animals can still be seen though many of them have been crushed.
To the south, where the soil appears moister, some stunted vegetation has begun
to grow but to the east the rocky land continues.
name: Rocky Land

desc:
Numerous rocks, both small and large, cover this arid ground as it nears the top
of the mountain from the south, making travel difficult and the land
inhospitable to vegetation. A small trail winds from the east on its way to the
mountain's peak. To the south the terrain appears similar to here. Rising in the
north is the peak of the mountain.
name: Steep Incline

desc:
From here, the top of the mountain, you can see much of the surrounding lands.
The southern slope gently descends, while the other sides of the mountain are
much steeper and more perilous. A small precipice is to the east, though it
appears somewhat unstable and would be difficult to reach.
name: Top of the Mountain

desc:
This side of the mountain is very steep and even an experienced climber would
find it nearly impossible to continue southward. The terrain is rough and barren
with no vegetation. Towards the south a tall mountain looms, overshadowing the
lands around.
name: Steep Mountainside

desc:
The ground here is rough and hard with numerous small stones embedded into the
surface although a few stunted, ancient junipers have managed to grow in the
softer spots. The land rises gently towards the south where it eventually forms
a steep mountain. To the north and east the remains of an old forest road can be
found.
name: Rising Slope

desc:
The road bends sharply here, continuing north and east. Southwards the ground
begins to rise towards some mountains. The surface of the road is hard packed,
indicating that it was once frequently travelled, although the small patches of
grass that are now growing make it doubtful the road has seen much use recently.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
A steep gloomy rock face rises to the south and west forcing the road to make a
sharp turn east and north of here. The southern wall of the rock face is sheer
and covered by some thick bushes while the west wall appears a bit gentler and
has a few cracks which make passage that way possible for a skilful climber.
name: Road beside the Mountain

desc:
This road is bordered by a gentle embankment of dirt and several small rocks to
the south. A tangled logging area covered with young saplings is to the north.
The road appears to be infrequently used since grass has managed to grow in many
sections.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Rocks of various sizes, as well as loose gravel, cover this embankment that
follows the road just north of here. There is no vegetation growing in this
austere ground for it is far too harsh to support plant life. A gloomy mountain
with a sheer face stands west and is unreachable from this direction.
name: Rocky Embankment

desc:
The ground here is particularly hard, and is unable to support much in the way
of vegetation. Only a few scraggly trees have managed to take root among the
stones that litter the ground. This rocky land rises northward and to the far
south a small pond has formed. In the east the soil becomes more fertile.
name: Stony Soil

desc:
The grass here has prospered and grown to dominate this smooth region which
gently declines eastward towards a crossing in the road. The soil becomes more
barren in the west but seems to burst with health in the eastern lands where the
river Anduin flows at its mightiest.
name: Grass beside the Road

desc:
The road descends gently eastward where the terrain is more fertile and able to
support its blooming vegetation. This poses a stark contrast with the land to
the west where the soil is harsh and the terrain is mostly barren. The surface
of the road is covered with short grass indicating it has seen little usage.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
The precipice is soft and brittle allowing many large fissures to form through
the passage of time. Several of the fissures have caved in over the years making
it apparent that they are both hollow and unstable. A few stunted pine trees
have managed to grow in the less harsh portions of the slope. The western
horizon is covered by a tremendous peak which obscures the view in that
direction as it rises from the ground.
name: Uneven Precipice

desc:
The head of this trail originates at the foot of the soft mountain slope, and
worms its way up to the precipice. The trail is tiled with small circular stones
and seems of an ancient origin, possibly constructed by mountain dwellers. A
short yellow grass traces the edge of the trail as it winds up towards the
precipice.
name: Winding Mountain Trail

desc:
You find yourself in the outskirts of the vast mountain forest that carpets the
valley side. The trees are more disperse in this area, opening room for a richer
and more diverse undergrowth. Especially prevalent are the tall, leafy ferns
that crowd around the thick trunks. Light filters in through the canopy of
leaves, casting whimsical patterns on the ground. Only at dusk, however, does
the forest show all its splendour when the waning light falls slanting over the
treetops and orange glints shimmer on the rims of the leaves.
name: Light Forest

desc:
The forest here thins, making way for some small bushes. The trees seem younger,
about twice as tall as an adult human, and the bushes bear small red berries
when in season. The foliage all around is thick and dark green in colour.
Resilient branches and leaves that snap back when pushed aside, creating a
confusing flurry, must slow travellers to these parts. A few hack marks made in
the plants to clear a path seems to have had no effect. The leaves are ever
growing and new leaves quickly replace the ones cut away.
name: Light Forest

desc:
In these borderlands between the forest and the vast open plains there still
grows an occasional tree among the small bushes and sturdy grasses. Westwards
the trees grow denser, while in all other directions the forest completely
vanishes.
name: Bordering Plains

desc:
From the looks of it this field was once fertile and lush with wheat; now almost
everything has withered away. Stalks of wheat lay clumped in piles on the
ground, slowly decomposing into the earth. Not far to the north is a bend where
the river turns and makes its way eastward. A dark forest looms across the field
a ways to the west.
name: Withering Field

desc:
A few solemn, scattered trees stand among the bushes and grasses in this area.
Like silent sentinels they seem to keep an ever vigilant watch for some unknown
menace, as if they were scouts or guardians of the forest that grows a short
distance to the north-west. Eastwards the plains open up as the Vale of the
Anduin gradually unfolds in front of you.
name: Guardian Trees

desc:
The land declines gently towards the east where a healthy, leafy brushwood
grows. The vegetation here is short, consisting mostly of grass with a few small
shrubs. The rising terrain to the west appears quite harsh while the eastern and
southern lands are more fertile.
name: Gentle Slope

desc:
Young slender trees slowly grow here, replacing those that were cut down in the
distant past. The soil is soft and nutritious offering a hospitable substratum
for the growing vegetation. The terrain southward seems to also be a former
habitat of trees and now contains many young saplings.
name: Woody Coppice

desc:
Several bountiful bushes cover this smooth region which has many kinds of
plants. The smaller plants, however, are left in the shadow of the bigger ones
and thus they struggle for life. Most of the soil appears quite fertile.
name: Brushwood

desc:
The ground here is filled with small bushes of a strange species. This type of
bush seems to grow only in this area for some mysterious reason. There are no
animal tracks in this area as if they shun these strange bushes and their slimy,
long reaching leaves. In a few places near the bushes some bones of small
animals are visible.
name: Among the Strange Bushes

desc:
The ambience of this clearing is very mysterious, with a strange mist rising
from the hollow lying to the south. The ground here is muddy and provides uneven
footing for travellers. A few puddles of water are scattered about. The horizon
is largely obscured by a strange mist.
name: Hazy Clearing

desc:
This is the border of a tremendous vale which opens to the east. The ground here
is covered with short grass and some bushes which are spread out across the
grass. The edge of the valley continues to the north while to the south there is
a vast plain covered by hay. A clearing lies cloaked in haze westward of here.
name: The Valley Edge

desc:
The plain is covered with short grass and a few small bushes. The ground
declines smoothly eastward where it joins a large valley filled with wildly
growing plants. Westward a mysterious mist rises from a large, strange looking
hollow that is covered with thick bushes.
name: Vast Plain

desc:
The vegetation in this bountiful valley is very luxuriant and bears a rich
growth of plants during the warm months of late spring and early summer. Land
such as this forms the perfect environment for plant eaters and the animals that
feed on them. The tracks of several animals are visible as well as a few small
bones.
name: Blooming Vale

desc:
The ground descends steeply from the west where the edge of the valley can be
seen. The deep, dark brown soil is very nutritious and forms the basis for the
many different kinds of plants growing here. The ground is mostly covered with
grass but a few small bushes and a young birch grove full of thin saplings are
also here.
name: Flourishing Valley

desc:
The grass, over a foot high, covers this flourishing vale between the lush
shrubs and several young birches that grow here. The land rises towards the west
where the edge of this valley is visible. This extensive vale continues to the
distant east where the great Anduin river flows.
name: Fertile Cove

desc:
The area is overshadowed by a pair of ancient trees with huge canopies that
provide shade here and to some brush in the east. The land declines sharply from
the west where the border of the vale is visible. Terrain similar to this region
continues far to the east with various small types of vegetation, like grass and
weeds, growing all around.
name: Shady Vale

desc:
From this point only a faint whispering sound can be heard from the river that
lies to the north. A large oak tree dominates the area, emitting a rotten smell
similar to that of unburied corpses. Some large trees far to the south cast dark
shadows upon much of this bushy plain.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The river slowly meanders ever onward to the east at a smooth, silent pace.
Occasionally a small fish can be seen leaping out of the water creating a brief
splash, breaking the serene silence. The usual water creatures go about their
business; insects skim the surface, fish swim in the current, and birds swoop
down to pluck a trout from the water. The river is bordered by plains to the
north and south. The ruins of a village can be spotted nearby to the north.
name: Silent River

desc:
Damp and silent is the garment worn by this abandoned ground. No being of
conscience could possibly desire to remain upon this dismal place for longer
than necessity demands. All that can be seen across the barren landscape is land
raped by fire. To the east the plains are far flourishing, yet from here they
too are silent. To the south-west the grasping claws of a rushing river can be
heard, seemingly yearning for someone or something to snatch from the riverbank.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The northern wall of this house is severely damaged, having buckled under the
weight of the roof. The north section of the roof has completely collapsed
leaving a sizeable hole above. Whatever caused the rampant destruction of the
village moved north from here leaving a large breach in the wall. Shattered
stones lie scattered all across the ground.
name: A Small Obliterated House

desc:
The remnants of an old stone wall stand sentinel here, preventing travel
southward from this point. In all other directions the plains stretch out toward
the horizon from the base of the wall creating a smooth, billowing grassy
expanse unbroken save for a tower far to the north-east.
name: Plains outside the Walls

desc:
The remains of a large old wall still stand here, blocking passage to the
south-east despite its crumbling state. The old wall follows a gentle curve,
making a circle that continues on to the east and south. Traces of debris and
piles of rock line its path.
name: Outside the Walls

desc:
Tall stone columns on either side of the road are all that is left intact of
this once lively village. The great gates, that once served as a border between
this city of Woodmen and the wilderness beyond, fell long ago. The city walls
are visibly weakened, with holes of varying sizes. Some of the holes are large
enough to allow medium-sized creatures to pass through. The gates themselves
appear to have taken quite a beating before they fell; there are large round
impact marks at about waist height, possibly from a battering ram. Splintered
fragments of the gate are scattered about the ground, and some larger chunks are
still bolted to the columns. Whatever force laid siege to this city, it must
have been quite massive.
name: Entrance to a Ruined Village

desc:
Just outside the old village walls this old field lies silently as a memory of
the old inhabitants of this area. A few wooden poles rise out of the ground, the
remains of a fence in a shape reminiscent of the grin of an old man that has
lost almost all his teeth. The field itself is slowly being reclaimed by the
surrounding plains, its man-sown crops fighting a valiant, but inevitably
losing, battle.
name: Ancient Fields

desc:
Silent and desolate best describe these plains that stretch out as far as the
eye can see. Like a vast brown carpet they welcome travellers to take a
leisurely stroll. However, this featureless area quickly becomes monotonous as
the only break in this bleak landscape is a small collection of collapsed huts,
probably the remains of an old farm slowly becoming as lifeless as the rest of
the surroundings.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
This is the western edge of a wide valley which runs north and south. To the far
east the mighty river Anduin flows in its centre. The lands to the east are
covered with many different kinds of vegetation, most of them flourishing. The
ground slopes sharply down from the edge to the centre of the Vale of Anduin.
The plains to the north appear quite barren.
name: The Valley Edge

desc:
The bushy terrain to the west ends here as the ground becomes flatter and the
bushes slowly die out. Eastwards, an enormous valley opens out and spreads far
to the east where it enfolds the river Anduin. Overall the vale is flourishing
with a large variety of vegetation. A huge rock, some twenty feet high, stands
at the edge of the valley.
name: The Valley Edge

desc:
The vegetation here has a lower density when compared to the lands westward. A
few medium-sized bushes grow here, leaving fairly wide routes between them. The
ground is abundantly covered by animal tracks and even a few humanoid prints are
visible on the surface. A wide valley opens out towards the east and continues
into the far distance.
name: Sparse Bushes

desc:
Scattered on the vast plains are a few patches of low growing bushes along with
some plants and creeping vines. Otherwise this area is dominated by weeds and
grasses not strongly bound by the plants. Occasionally a light blowing wind
stirs up some dust which slowly settles back to the ground covering the
greenery.
name: Dusty Plains

desc:
The proximity of this place to the river just north-east of here has created a
rich and varied environment where various plants, weeds and grasses compete for
the mineral rich space. A few single trees stand spread out along the bank of
the river, throwing their small shadows across the otherwise open plains.
name: Lush Plains

desc:
The trail meanders along, slowly leading eastwards. There is little sign of wear
on the ground leaving only a faint rut to indicate the path upon which grass is
taking hold. A river rushing nearby to the south fills the air with the furious
churning sound of fast-flowing water. The sound seems fainter to the north,
where the quiet plains stretch out into the distance.
name: Abandoned Trail

desc:
The land here is barren, with a mixture of large boulders and gravel scattered
about. The rocks are all that provides even a variety of colour. This area seems
quite inhospitable to any kind of life, be it plants or animals. To the east
there seem to be the ruins of a small village in the distance. To the south
there is an old disused trail.
name: Rocky Plains

desc:
Several young pines grow on this vast field, shooting off from the older trees
in the west. This is the perfect spot for new trees to grow, a large flourishing
field with nourishment from the river that passes by to the west. Many full and
round pinecones litter the ground, evidence that the trees are quite healthy. If
even half of the cones sprout this field could grow to be forest.
name: Pine Infested Landscape

desc:
This small trail near the riverbank is covered in high grass indicating it
hasn't seen much use in quite some time. The trail continues its journey
eastwards for a while, before coming to an abrupt halt before the fallen gates
of a ruined village. From the south the sound of rushing water can be heard,
presumably the roaring river to the west.
name: Abandoned Trail

desc:
Crossing the swift waters of the river below an old and creaking rope-bridge
passes the wild river here. Allowing safe passage for the worn and weary
traveller, the bridge safely carries anyone across as it bypasses the strong and
powerful currents and eddies that otherwise would be a harsh threat.
name: Old Rope Bridge

desc:
This small path is almost completely covered up by thick, waist-high grass. The
trail leads from a large river in the north and vanishes as it travels south. To
the west is a withered field of wheat, and a rushing river can be seen
south-east.
name: Vanishing Path

desc:
Various plants battling for space mix here into one big tangled mass. It is hard
to tell exactly what plants make up this entanglement since there is no way to
separate them all. Clearly there are some wild grasses and herbs, along with
some wildflowers, all corralled by several groups of shrubs. Far to the west a
dense and dark mass of trees line the horizon, while to the east the plains
stretch out to the horizon.
name: Tangled Plain

desc:
These plains are a patchwork of varied vegetation. A single tree stands in a
small cluster of bushes, while a dense group of brushwood is slowly creeping in
from the south. To the northeast the vegetation slowly diminishes, giving way to
vast open areas of grass.
name: Brushy Plains

desc:
Large bushes with thick leaves grow more tightly-packed, forming a dense
cluster, because of the excellent soil. The terrain south of here is made of the
same soil and is covered in similar bushes. While eastwards the vegetation
merely thins, to the west it appears scanty.
name: Brushwood

desc:
The entire ceiling of this great hall has collapsed, littering the floor with
stones of various sizes. Sections of the walls have also been smashed in and
several gaps are easily large enough to allow light into the room. Other rooms
once led off this one, but nothing of those rooms remains. Numerous bones jut
out from under the fallen rubble and a couple of shattered skeletons can be
seen, making this room look like a mass grave. To the north there is another
ruined hall.
name: Crumbled Hall

desc:
From the scattered stones one can tell that this huge building once underwent
some sort of large-scale catastrophe. The basic structure seems to have endured
surprisingly well apart from the fallen mezzanine and the burned furniture. Many
blocks of the former roof can be seen scattered among the skeletal remains on
the ground. To the south there lies another hall which appears to have crumbled
more extensively than this one.
name: Scorched Mansion

desc:
In the centre of this destroyed and ash-covered district stands a colossal well,
some ten feet in diameter. The ring of the well is built of large granite blocks
many of which have become loose or have fallen from the well ring. A large winch
with a frail rope and wooden bucket stands above the well, seemingly still in
workable condition.
name: At the Broken Well

desc:
The extent of the mass destruction that was inflicted upon this village years
ago is still easily visible when viewing the remains of the dwellings. However,
time and the ravages of the weather have worked at the village and have softened
some of the harshness of the destroyed structures. The strong stonewalls which
surround the village are surprisingly well preserved. The only building that
seems to have endured the ravage in some fashion is a large structure standing
in the west. To the south there lies a massive but shattered well.
name: Ruined Yard

desc:
Three straw pallets lie on the floor, and although they don't look extremely
comfortable, you guess that they must be much better than sleeping on the bare
floorboards. A chair sits in the corner, and a small lamp is resting on a little
wooden box in the middle of the southern wall. A large chest sits at the other
end of the room, and this must contain the possessions of the hunters who own
this abode.
name: Sleeping Quarters

desc:
Several crushed skeletons lie on the bottom of this dried up well. The well has
become a mass grave for the previous citizens of this destroyed village. A few
stones of the well ring have fallen down into here and crushed the pitiful
corpses further. The walls of the well are rather rugged making it possible to
climb out.
name: Bottom of the Well

desc:
The river rushes quickly, speeding away from its roots in the western forest.
Some leaves and twigs float in the water, little pieces of the forest it carries
with it like mementos of its origin. All this river has collected is swiftly
carried away from here, as the river continues on to some destination in the
east. Most of these seeds of the forest will be left along the shores of the
river before reaching the river's end.
name: Fast Flowing River

desc:
Large sturdy branches form the base of this great larch that is perfectly shaped
like an enormous evergreen tree. It quite possibly serves as a shelter for those
hiding from ferocious animals, or as a temporary lodging in the forest. The
hungry sounds of what might be wolves can be heard close by.
name: At the Top of a Tall Larch

desc:
A wide vista opens up for a person on this tall rock, making it possible for
many to see the river Anduin flowing peacefully in the far east. The sides of
the rock are sheer except the western edge where descent seems possible. The
surface of the rock is covered with the excrement of birds.
name: On Top of the Huge Rock

desc:
You are standing on a thick branch. The thick mass of leaves blocks the sun out.
Far to the north is a small stream, to the east a road and beyond it a very dark
forest. The landscape to the south is not versatile, rocks and stones are
dominating. To the west there is a very steep mountain. Crunch... you stepped on
a little bone. Who uses the branch as a dining table?
name: In a Tree

desc:
This path has not been used for a very long time. It leads west into the opening
in the side of the mountain. Just outside the opening, where water and mud meet,
there are some very big and deep footprints. From time to time the path is
totally flooded so one has to swim.
name: Flooded Path

desc:
You are in a small cave room just inside the mountain. You hear a lot of
grumbling noises from the large well-lit cave to the west. The cave seems to
have been a mine once, bearing the marks of picks and being quite accurately cut
out in the mountain. However, you cannot believe that the skilled masons who
once made this cave still live here. Definitely, something else has taken this
cave as its home. There is a lot of water on the ground, slowly flowing from the
north to the east.
name: Cave

desc:
You feel a terrible stench from the piles of debris lying in the corners of the
cave. This is the home of big and ugly cave trolls, which are among the most
fearsome creatures in this part of Middle-earth. Scattered around are the
remnants of unlucky animals, humans, dwarves, elves and even orcs upon whom the
trolls have feasted. The only way out seems to be through the large opening to
the east.
name: Trolls' Lair

desc:
You have found an old, long abandoned mining tunnel. The ceiling is rather low,
forcing tall creatures to bend down to be able to move. The tunnel leads east
and upwards deeper into the mountain. There is a lot of water on the ground in
this part of the shaft.
name: Cave

desc:
A long time ago silver and iron were gathered here to be loaded on mounts and
taken away. Now the cave is empty, and it feels strange to have a place like
this deep inside the mountain.
name: Abandoned Storage Cave

desc:
Though short grass and a few small bushes still manage to cover this plain, many
of them have been trampled by animals. Most of the moss that once grew here has
wilted although a few tussocks of it still remain. The grasslands continue to
the west and north while to the east the land begins to be dominated by bushes.
name: Grassland

desc:
The land here is entirely covered by grass with a few small bushes and richly
coloured flowers pushing up between the stalks. A few low mounds are scattered
about and blanketed with a moss. The terrain has more bushes to the west but the
grass here continues into the east and north.
name: Grassland

desc:
Different kinds of bushes cover this smooth plain, which is south of a mud-
covered trail. A few small rocks lie across the exposed surface and some earth-
worms are wriggling on the muddy surface. The land continues to be covered by
bushes to the west but turns grassy in the east.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
The plains here are very soft, covered by numerous large bushes growing close
enough to each other to conceal the ground with their giant leaves. A collapsed
guard tower with blackened walls rises to the west where it stands next to a
burned out village. A muddy trail to the north passes near here and comes to an
end in front of the ruined village. This bushy region continues eastward.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
The collapse of most of the supporting walls, the broken ladders, and the
dilapidated ceiling of this wrecked tower makes reaching the upper floor nearly
impossible. The floor is littered with blackened bricks that are highlighted by
several white bones that stick out from underneath. A massive, but worn-out
stonewall can be seen through the hole in the western wall.
name: Collapsed Guard Tower

desc:
The vegetation here is very patchy, with only small areas of plants which are
mostly grass. A few small withered-looking bushes have managed to take root in
the surrounding area. To the north-east is the gateway to a burned down village
and a collapsed guard tower can be seen to the east.
name: Patchy Ground

desc:
Many flat rocks cover this plain which appears very barren with almost no
vegetation. Only a few tussocks of dry grass can be seen growing from the
surface. The ground has fewer stones to the north where a dry-looking plain can
be seen. Farther to the north several mountains loom.
name: Stony Plain

desc:
Peaks of swaying stems of grass lie like a blanket over the fields. Beneath, a
rich earth feeds the vegetation. Smells of herbs and dirt, and a sense of soft
moisture fill the air.
name: Grazing Fields

desc:
When sun or moon shines the reflected light plays in the fields. It jumps from
straw to straw, changing their hues as it goes. The sway of the grass helps,
making the scenery even more spectacular. Beneath this, insects have their homes
among the gravel and dirt, digging tunnels and feeding on whatever they can
claim.
name: Blisters of Green

desc:
The grass rolls out in all directions as a carpet covering the land. An
occasional rock or lonesome tree can be spotted, but very little disturbs the
rule of the grass. Deep within the green tangles white and yellow flowers
struggle to spring up and reach for the beams of the sun.
name: Rolling Greens

desc:
The green tangles hold a firm grip of the earth, letting few or none of the
beams from the sun reach down to their roots. Close to the ground there is
little growth, except for the close-packed stems of grass reaching for the sky.
Gazing out over the fields flowers of white and yellow dot the green, and in the
west a drier landscape reaches out.
name: Rampant Grasslands

desc:
Here the ground follows a gentle descent to the south. Streaks of shallow
ditches run across the land letting the water flow towards the lower lands in
the south. The grass here uses this water to flourish in green, and along the
sides of the shallows white flowers grow closely in patches.
name: Gentle Wet Slope

desc:
Shallow natural furrows run from north to south across the green fields.
Occasional rains fill them with water travelling to the south. There is however
a constant supply of water in these trenches as they are fed with dew and mist
from the endless fields in the north. Venturing upwards to the east takes the
traveller into a maze of tangles towards a sharp slope in the fields.
name: Thriving Slope

desc:
Flourishing green grass stretches out, flowing over the fields. Small bushes and
tangles snare the land to the east, but in this area the swaying grass has a
firm grip of the land. Natural shallow ditches run across the fields in a
disordered pattern. Most of these paths are dried out, with only wet mud to show
for the water that once ran there. Even during rains, the ground is thirsty
enough to not let any water flow away. To the east the path is blocked by a
tangle of brown branches.
name: Rich Rows of Hay

desc:
Between the stems of the green grass, snakes, rats and other small animals may
go about their business. The hay rattles occasionally in the wind or when
disturbed by something deep in the thick green. These lands seem satisfied with
water and sun, flourishing in their growth.
name: Whirling Rows of Grass

desc:
Here, as in the fields around, the grass grows in hundred different hues of
green. All straws of the hay have their unique shades like swaying individuals.
But growing together as they do the result is a rainbow of greens covering the
land. Brown herbs and yellow and white flowers can be spotted within the deep
sea of grass by a keen eye.
name: Blistering Hues of Green

desc:
In all directions the green grass keeps a firm grip on the land. Far in the
north-west horizon however the peaks of mountains can be spotted by the keen eye
gazing down through mists and clouds. In this area though there is little sight
of slopes or peaks, and this form stretches far away in the distance.
name: Thriving Swards

desc:
Looking out over the fields rolling away into the horizon offers a sight only
comparable to an ocean. The colours of the ocean have been switched from the
marine blue to green and brown, but still undulate and shift like waves on a
frantic sea. The earth beneath the grass is soft and even soggy in places, but
solid enough to not give way when rain and snow falls.
name: Flourishing Lea

desc:
Moisture and wealth of growth dominates the fields. The level landscape is
covered with a thick, swaying coat of straws in a vast range of shapes and
colours. This area serves as home, playground and pantry for its inhabitants.
The earth is soft and rich, and fills the air with a smell of soft dirt.
name: Prosperous Green

desc:
The carpet of grass and plants stretches over the landscape, shifting from the
lightest shades of brown, to sharp, almost luminous hues of green. As the old
plants decay they are replaced by fresh crops of grass, forming layers of either
seasoned or keen stems. The decaying smell fills the air, mixing with the
piquant scent of new growing.
name: Lush Grasslands

desc:
The fields are coloured in green and brown, shifting and flowing through the
landscape. Below in the nestled floor of decaying brown grass, ants and other
hard working insects rearrange the miniature scenery as they see fit. To the
south a sharp ridge quickly climbs and reaches its top. Beyond this high ground
sun-burnt grass and brown reeds quickly replace the lush greens. The ridge is
covered in rocks and gravel, serving as home for numerous insects and small
reptiles. To the east gravel and a large stone has formed a shelter protecting
the ground from wind and rain.
name: Beneath a Steep Ridge

desc:
The luscious cover of grass fills the air with scents of herbs and dirt. The
plain stretches out and touches the horizon in all directions. To the south a
steep slope quickly works its way up to an impassable sharp top. On the ascent
the plants and grass crave the sun, but their location on the north-faced slope
only grants their wish during a few short hours every day. To the west large
stones and gravel fallen from the side of the slope effectively block the path.
name: Luscious Greens at a Narrow Crest

desc:
The ever flowing green is abruptly interrupted here by long since overgrown
squares of pasture. They are framed with what once could be called ditches in a
pattern far too symmetrical to be made by nature itself. The ground is level and
the elsewhere so mandatory gravel and small rocks are nowhere to be seen. The
shallow ditches are soggy and overgrown; apparently rain still gathers in their
lines and a thirsty wanderer will be able to find enough here to dampen his
need. In the south a sharp ridge cuts through the land, creating a grey scar of
rocks and gravel in the fields.
name: Old Pastures at a Steep Ridge

desc:
Small squares of fields, regulated by shallow overgrown ditches, break the
flowing dominance of grass and herbs. While the stems of green and brown still
cover the landscape, here it has been ordered into tidy shapes. It is obvious
that these pastures has long since been abandoned, but they nevertheless still
serve as a haven for more craving plants and herbs, with rich earth and gravel
free ground. In the grass-filled trenches, water is collected as rain falls.
name: An Overgrown Pasture

desc:
Swaying grass, layered with brown and green in different heights and
appearances, rules the land. To the west a more ordered line of fields can be
seen, as if placed there by hand, but here the unordered scheme of nature takes
its grasp of the earth again. A gentle slope stretches up in the south, and
beyond its face more dried out scenery can be seen.
name: Spreading Fields

desc:
This field is covered with golden grass reaching to the knees of a full-grown
man, and in places even higher. The straws grow closer to each other here than
in the surrounding areas, swaying when the wind blows as golden waves in the
grass. Every footstep here is followed by a small cloud of dust, disturbed by
the movement.
name: Thirsty Hays

desc:
Close to the ground the golden straws of grass create a labyrinth in the dust
and gravel. The earth is cracked in places, and serves as home for numerous
insects and small reptiles. In the north greener fields resembling pastures
cover the land, while in the southwest a stony ledge stubbornly cuts the land.
name: Gravelled Earth

desc:
This field flourishes in its own richness; the land is alive with animals using
it as home and hunting ground. An occasional bird might be spotted, casting its
shadow on the green grass, along with a quick rabbit running through the stems,
or a snake hiding its presence among the gravel. To the north the landscape
shades in gold and yellow, and in the south the land is sickened with the
excessive supply of water.
name: Opulent Grasslands

desc:
In the north a steep ridge cuts through the landscape and continues westwards
while it in the east gently levels out with the landscape. It lets this area
keep the rain that falls, and the grass can offer itself some shade during early
and late hours of the day. While the land further in the south becomes soggy and
damp, this area keeps a good balance and the green can flourish. The smell of
herbs and flowers fills the air, but for the keen nose a scent of fungi and
wetness flows in from the south.
name: Rich Greens

desc:
Yellow and golden straws spread like a carpet over the fields. To the south and
east their richness increases into a far greener appearance. Water running from
the cracked earth in the north makes the land in the south wet and misty. Gazing
even further the contours of the Gladden Fields paint their dark shapes on the
horizon.
name: Dust Filled Acres

desc:
Dirt and dust flows through the air, reflecting any light from sun or moon as
countless fire-flies. In the northeast a sharp, prominent ridge runs over the
fields. The northern side is steep and rocky, while the southern side slopes
gently downwards, placing the thirsting plants in the cross-line of the sun,
parching their presence.
name: Parched Slope in the Plains

desc:
In the north a sharp ridge runs from east to west, filled with hazardous rocks
and gravel. Beyond it rich green fields stretch out into the horizon, but here
the earth is harder and the surface is covered with dust and gravel between the
yellow straws of grass. The busy insects are ever present, but the sound flowing
in the air seems damp and lazy.
name: Dry Slope

desc:
Climbing a daring crest to the north, the green grass turns into a mesh of dry
straws, sloping down into the south. The slant is sharp and mostly noticeable by
the occasional shifting of rocks on the slope. There is nothing here that
provides shelter from the sun, and the rain that falls quickly flows away on the
hard earth.
name: On a Crest in the Fields

desc:
The earth is dry and dusty, but in the south where the slope levels out into the
rest of the land, the intense green colours of fresh grass reclaim their hold of
the scene. Small flowers and plants fight for their presence among the ruling
grass, offering a change of colour in the otherwise so sectarian hues.
name: Gentle Slope

desc:
The dry slanting ground levels out with the green fields to the south. A large
rock covered in dust and gravel, but with little signs of moss and lichen, has
seemingly scrambled down on the long slope and come to a rest here, among golden
straws and crushed gravel. The hay has embraced the boulder and crawled half-way
up its sides.
name: Rock on the Dried Descent

desc:
This mining tunnel was built by dwarves long time ago. The tunnels to north and
south are caved in and the only options are to go back or continue eastwards.
The wall to the north is beginning to crumble, and clear, cold water gushes
forth from cracks in the stone.
name: Deserted Mine Shaft
